en: to pull low one's hat or cap

examples.en: I pulled my hat down low and went out.
I pulled my cap down deep to hide my face.

examples.ko: 야구 모자를 눌러쓴 남자가 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: A man with his baseball cap pulled low looked at me.
It's cold, so I pull my wool hat down over my ears.
If I pull my hat down in the morning, my hair gets flattened.
It was raining, so I pulled my raincoat hood down low.

explain: 모자 같은 것을 깊이 내려서 쓸 때 쓰고, 보통 '푹'과 잘 어울려요. 글씨를 힘주어 꾹꾹 쓸 때도 '눌러쓰다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 비가 와서 모자를 푹 눌러쓰고 걸었어요.
phrases.en: It was raining, so I walked with my hat pulled low.
phrases.nuance_ko: '푹'과 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most frequent pairing, with 푹.
phrases.en_equiv: to pull a hat down low

phrases.example: 모자를 눌러쓰고 있어서 얼굴이 안 보여요.
phrases.en: He's wearing his cap low, so I can't see his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모자를 내려 쓴 상태가 이어지는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the ongoing state of wearing a cap low.
phrases.en_equiv: to be wearing it pulled low

phrases.example: 편지를 꾹꾹 눌러써서 종이에 자국이 남았어요.
phrases.en: I wrote the letter pressing hard, so marks stayed on the paper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글씨를 힘주어 쓰는 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for writing with firm, pressed strokes.

explain_en: It is used when you pull a hat or similar item down low, often with '푹'. It is also used for writing with firm pressure, pressing hard on the paper.

examples.ko: 동생이 거짓말을 하자 엄마가 도끼눈으로 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: When my sister lied, Mom glared at her.
Please don't glare at me like that.

examples.ko: 친구가 도끼눈을 하고 저를 노려봐서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: My friend glared at me with sharp eyes, and it was scary.
They asked in an accusing glare, so it was hard to answer.
My boss checked the documents with a sharp, stern look.

examples.ko: 아이들이 도끼눈을 한 채 서로 눈치를 봤어요.
examples.en: The kids eyed each other with glaring looks.

explain: 화가 나거나 미워서 눈을 모나게 뜨고 볼 때 쓰는 말이에요. '도끼눈을 뜨다', '도끼눈으로 보다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '째려보다'가 있는데, 도끼눈은 표정과 눈매를 그릴 때 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The teacher looked around the classroom with glaring eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어가 가장 자주 쓰이는 형태로, 화난 눈매를 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form of the word, meaning to make an angry, sharp-eyed look.

phrases.en: He glared at me with hostile eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '노려보다'와 함께 쓰면 미운 마음이 더 세게 느껴져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 노려보다 makes the hostile feeling stronger.

phrases.en: My younger sibling glared at me, and it was scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 일상 대화에서 더 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word with a similar meaning that is more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: This describes eyes opened sharply in anger or dislike, used as '도끼눈을 뜨다' or '도끼눈으로 보다'. '째려보다' is similar, but 도끼눈 sounds more natural when describing the look on someone's face.

en: the nape; the back of the neck

examples.en: The back of my neck suddenly felt chilly, so I looked behind me.
The teacher grabbed the child who was messing around by the back of the neck.
The back of my neck got bright red from the sun at the beach.
The back of my neck is stiff, so I want to get a massage.
The cat carried its kitten by the scruff of the neck.
With my hair tied up high, the back of my neck feels cool.

explain: 목 뒤쪽 아래 부분이에요. '목덜미'라고도 하는데, 일상에서는 둘 다 자주 써요. '뒷덜미를 잡다/잡히다'는 비유로도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 몰래 숙제를 베끼다가 선생님께 뒷덜미를 잡혔어요.
phrases.en: to get caught
phrases.nuance_ko: 잘못이나 약점이 들켜서 붙잡히거나 꼼짝 못 하게 되는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a mistake or weak point is discovered and you are caught or cornered.

explain_en: It is the lower back part of the neck, and it is also called '목덜미'; both are common in daily speech. '뒷덜미를 잡다/잡히다' is also widely used figuratively.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 들창코라서 웃을 때 더 귀여워요.
examples.en: My little brother has an upturned nose, so he looks even cuter when he smiles.
I was teased for having an upturned nose when I was little.
Piglets have such cute snub noses.
I take after my dad, so I have an upturned nose too.
That actor is popular even though he has an upturned nose.
That puppy has a snub nose and round eyes.

explain: '매부리코', '납작코'처럼 코 모양을 가리키는 말 중 하나예요. 귀엽다는 느낌으로 말하기도 하지만, 남의 외모를 말할 때는 놀리는 말로 들릴 수 있으니 조심해요.

phrases.en: My puppy has an upturned nose.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 동물의 코 모양을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can describe the nose shape of animals as well as people.

phrases.en: When I smile, the tip of my nose lifts up a little.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들창코'를 풀어서 부드럽게 말한 표현이라서 놀리는 느낌이 적어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to describe it, with less of a teasing tone.

phrases.en: My friend's upturned nose is their charm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 코 모양을 좋은 뜻으로, 그 사람의 특징처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the nose shape in a positive way, as someone's distinctive feature.
phrases.en_equiv: the upturned nose is one's charm

explain_en: It is one of several words for nose shapes, like '매부리코' (hooked nose) and '납작코' (flat nose). Some people say it affectionately as cute, but it can sound like teasing when you talk about someone's looks, so be careful.

en: to be groggy; to be hazy; to be dazed

examples.en: I stayed up all night, so my head feels foggy.

examples.ko: 감기약을 먹은 뒤에 정신이 몽롱해서 계속 졸았어요.
examples.en: After taking cold medicine, my mind was hazy and I kept dozing off.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나면 한동안 몽롱한 상태로 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: When I wake up in the morning, I sit there in a daze for a while.
The foggy dawn road looked hazy and dreamlike.

examples.ko: 몽롱하지 않으려고 아침에 커피를 한 잔 마셨어요.
examples.en: I had a cup of coffee in the morning so I wouldn't feel groggy.

examples.ko: 꿈에서 막 깬 것처럼 한참 몽롱했어요.
examples.en: I felt dazed for a long while, as if I had just woken from a dream.

explain: 졸리거나 아파서 정신이 흐릿할 때 써요. '멍하다'는 생각 없이 가만히 있는 느낌이고, '몽롱하다'는 반쯤 잠든 듯 의식이 흐린 느낌이에요. 안개나 불빛처럼 분위기가 흐릿하고 꿈같을 때도 써요.

phrases.en: I took cold medicine and my mind feels hazy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몽롱하다'와 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 졸리거나 아플 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, used when sleepy or ill.

phrases.example: 안개 낀 호수의 몽롱한 분위기가 좋았어요.
phrases.en: I liked the dreamy atmosphere of the foggy lake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분위기나 풍경이 흐릿하고 꿈같을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when a scene or mood feels vague and dreamlike.

phrases.en: I was sleepy and things in front of me gradually got hazy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어지다'를 붙여 점점 흐릿해지는 변화를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어지다' shows a gradual change to hazy.

explain_en: Mind or consciousness feels foggy, like half asleep; not about room light. It is used when your mind is blurry from sleepiness or illness. '멍하다' means spacing out with an empty mind, while '몽롱하다' feels like being half asleep with clouded awareness. It can also describe hazy, dreamlike scenes such as fog or soft lights.

t90.ax: I stayed up all night, so my head feels foggy.

en: to be bald; to be smooth and bare

examples.ko: 머리를 너무 짧게 깎아서 머리가 민숭민숭해요.
examples.en: I cut my hair so short that my head looks bare.
The top of my father's head is getting thinner and thinner.
There's no grass, so the hill looks bare.
I shaved my beard clean so my chin is smooth.
The baby's head is still bare.
The mountain with all its trees cut down looks bare.

explain: 머리카락, 수염, 풀, 나무처럼 있어야 할 것이 없어서 반반하게 드러난 모습이에요. 머리, 턱, 산, 언덕 같은 곳에 써요. 비슷한 말로 '맨송맨송하다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I put a hat on my bald head.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민숭민숭하다'를 꾸밈말(-ㄴ)로 바꿔서 명사 앞에 붙인 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the modifier form (-ㄴ) of 민숭민숭하다, placed before a noun.

phrases.en: My head became bald as I got older.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 있던 것이 없어져서 점점 반반하게 변하는 과정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This describes the process of gradually becoming bare as something that used to be there disappears.

phrases.en: I shaved my beard, so my chin is smooth and bare.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같은 말이에요. 털이 없는 곳에 쓰고 말하는 느낌은 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a near-synonym used for places where hair is missing, with a similar feel.

explain_en: It describes a surface that looks smooth and exposed because something expected, such as hair, a beard, grass or trees, is missing. It is used for heads, chins, mountains and hills. '맨송맨송하다' is a similar word.

en: to be glossy; to be sleek; to be glib

examples.en: I put oil on my hair, and now it's glossy.
My newly bought shoes are shining sleekly.
Don't be fooled by his slick way of talking.
The fur looks glossy and shiny.
I ate oily food, so my lips were shiny.
It's only shiny on the outside; it's empty inside.

explain: 윤기가 나고 매끈해 보일 때 써요. '번지르르하다'와 모음만 다른 비슷한 말로, 반지르르가 조금 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요. '겉만 반지르르하다'처럼 겉모습만 좋은 것을 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The sleek, glossy hair looks great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 형태예요. 윤기 나는 머리를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifying form before a noun, often used for glossy hair.

phrases.en: I didn't wash my hair, so it isn't glossy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 윤기가 없다는 뜻이지만 '지저분하다'는 뜻은 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form; it means not glossy, not necessarily messy.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 말만 반지르르하고 행동은 없어요.
phrases.en: That person is all smooth talk with no action.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이나 말만 좋고 속은 그렇지 않다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means good only on the outside or in words, but not inside.
phrases.en_equiv: to be slick only on the surface

explain_en: Use it for something that looks shiny and smooth. It is a close relative of '번지르르하다' differing only in vowels, with 반지르르 feeling a bit smaller and lighter. It is also used for things that only look good outside, as in '겉만 반지르르하다'.

t90.ax: The fur looks glossy and shiny.

examples.ko: 배란이 규칙적이지 않아서 병원에서 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: My ovulation isn't regular, so I got tested at the hospital.

examples.ko: 배란일을 계산해 주는 앱을 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm using an app that calculates my ovulation day.

examples.ko: 배란 시기에는 몸이 조금 피곤할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Around ovulation, your body can feel a bit tired.

examples.ko: 배란 후에는 체온이 약간 올라간다고 해요.
examples.en: They say body temperature rises slightly after ovulation.

examples.ko: 스트레스를 많이 받으면 배란이 늦어질 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard ovulation can be delayed when you're under a lot of stress.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 배란 주기를 기록해 보라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to keep a record of my ovulation cycle.

explain: '배란일', '배란기', '배란 주기'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서 자주 써요. 건강 검진이나 임신 준비, 생리 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '배란이 되다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I went to the hospital timed to my ovulation day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배란이 일어나는 날을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The day on which ovulation occurs.

phrases.example: 배란기에는 몸 상태가 조금 달라질 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Your body can feel a little different during ovulation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배란이 일어나는 시기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The period when ovulation takes place.

phrases.example: 스트레스를 받으면 배란이 잘 안 될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: When you're stressed, ovulation may not happen well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배란이 일어나는지 아닌지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether ovulation happens or not.

explain_en: It is often combined with other words, as in '배란일', '배란기' and '배란 주기'. It comes up in health checkups, talk about trying to conceive, and menstrual cycles. People usually say '배란이 되다'.

examples.en: I was so embarrassed that my face turned red.

examples.ko: 매운 걸 먹으면 얼굴이 금방 벌게져요.
examples.en: My face quickly turns red when I eat spicy food.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 코가 벌게졌어요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day and my nose turned red.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 귀까지 벌게진 채 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: He shouted with his ears red with anger.

examples.ko: 햇볕에 오래 있었더니 팔이 벌게져서 따가워요.
examples.en: I was in the sun for a long time and my arm is red and stinging.
I cried for a long time until my eyes were red.

explain: 부끄러움, 화, 추위, 햇볕 때문에 얼굴이나 피부가 붉어질 때 써요. '빨개지다'보다 어둡고 탁한 붉은색 느낌이에요. '벌겋다'가 기본형 형용사이고 '벌게지다'는 그렇게 변하는 과정을 말해요.

phrases.en: My nose turned red from the cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 밝고 선명한 붉은색이라서 '벌게지다'보다 가벼운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A brighter, clearer red, so it feels lighter than 벌게지다.

phrases.en: My shoulders are red from the sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벌게지다'가 변하는 과정이라면 '벌겋다'는 이미 그 색인 상태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 벌게지다 is the process of changing; 벌겋다 is already being that color.

phrases.example: 벌게진 얼굴로 아무 말도 못 했어요.
phrases.en: With a flushed face, I couldn't say anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 변한 뒤의 얼굴을 설명할 때 '-ㄴ'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the -ㄴ form to describe a face after it has changed color.

explain_en: Duller, deeper red; face flushes from shame, anger or alcohol. It is used when the face or skin turns red from embarrassment, anger, cold or sun. The red feels darker and duller than with '빨개지다'. '벌겋다' is the adjective, and '벌게지다' describes the change into that color.

examples.en: He looks so sickly that I'm worried.
I put on makeup to hide how sick I looked.
He doesn't look ill, but he seems to have no energy.
He came to work with a sickly-looking face.
After resting a few days, the sickly look has mostly gone too.

examples.ko: 친구의 병색에 놀라서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was so shocked at my friend's sickly look that I couldn't say a word.

explain: '병색이 짙다', '병색이 있다', '병색이 가시다'처럼 써요. 몸이 안 좋아 보이는 얼굴빛을 말해서, 일상에서는 '안색이 안 좋다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Grandfather's face looks very ill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픈 기색이 얼굴에 뚜렷하게 보일 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical pairing for when signs of illness are clearly visible on the face.

phrases.en: After resting a few days, the sickly look went away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파 보이던 얼굴빛이 좋아졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the unwell look on the face has gone.

phrases.en: You look pale today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 병색을 쉽게 말하는 표현이에요. 상대에게도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday way to say this, and it can be said to the person directly.

explain_en: Look of illness on the face or body (얼굴에 병색) It appears as '병색이 짙다', '병색이 있다' or '병색이 가시다'. It describes a face that looks unwell, and in daily talk people also say '안색이 안 좋다'.

examples.en: My strength declined as I got older.
My grandfather's health has weakened, so he goes out less.

examples.ko: 한때 강했던 나라도 힘이 쇠하는 때가 와요.
examples.en: Even a once-strong country has a time when its power fades.
My eyesight is gradually getting worse, so I changed my glasses.

examples.ko: 병을 앓고 나서 체력이 많이 쇠했나 봐요.
examples.en: I guess my stamina dropped a lot after being ill.

examples.ko: 쇠해 가는 마을에 젊은 사람들이 돌아오고 있어요.
examples.en: Young people are coming back to the declining village.

explain: 기운, 힘, 세력이 약해질 때 써요. 반대말은 '흥하다'나 '성하다'예요. 보통 '기력이 쇠하다', '체력이 쇠하다'처럼 몸이나 힘 이야기에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: Your stamina declines as you get older.
phrases.nuance_ko: '체력, 기력, 힘'과 함께 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used with 체력, 기력, and 힘.

phrases.example: 그 나라의 힘이 점점 쇠해 갔어요.
phrases.en: That country's power gradually declined.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~아/어 가다'를 붙이면 조금씩 약해지는 모습이 나타나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '~아/어 가다' shows a gradual weakening.

phrases.en: A company has times of rising and declining.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '흥하다'와 짝으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is paired with the opposite word 흥하다.

explain_en: Formal, literary verb for strength or health fading with age (기력이 쇠하다). It is used when energy, strength or influence grows weaker. Its opposites are '흥하다' and '성하다'. It often appears in phrases about the body or strength, such as '기력이 쇠하다' and '체력이 쇠하다'.

t90.ax: My strength declined as I got older.

examples.en: I hurt my Achilles tendon while running.
My Achilles tendon was strained, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 운동하기 전에 아킬레스건을 충분히 풀어 주세요.
examples.en: Stretch your Achilles tendon well before exercising.
English pronunciation is my Achilles' heel.
That company's Achilles' heel is its lack of technology.

examples.ko: 상대 팀은 우리의 아킬레스건을 정확히 알고 공격했어요.
examples.en: The other team knew our weak point exactly and attacked it.

explain: 발뒤꿈치 위의 힘줄이라는 뜻 외에, 비유로 '가장 치명적인 약점'을 말해요. '약점'과 비슷하지만 전체를 흔들 수 있는 가장 큰 약점이라는 느낌이 강해요. 몸 이야기인지 비유인지는 문맥으로 구분해요.

phrases.en: That question touched his Achilles' heel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비유로 쓸 때 가장 많이 나오는 표현으로, 가장 아픈 약점을 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common figurative use: touching someone's greatest weakness.

phrases.example: 축구 선수가 아킬레스건이 끊어져서 수술을 받았어요.
phrases.en: The soccer player's Achilles tendon ruptured and he had surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 힘줄을 말할 때 쓰는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the literal use, about the body's tendon.

phrases.en: This team's weak point is defense.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아킬레스건'보다 가벼운 약점이고 어디에나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter, more general word for a weakness than 'Achilles' heel'.

explain_en: Besides the tendon above the heel, it figuratively means one's most critical weakness. It is close to '약점' but suggests the biggest weak spot that could bring everything down. Context tells you whether it is about the body or a metaphor.

examples.en: I had surgery before the cancer cells spread.
The test showed there were no cancer cells.

examples.ko: 의사들은 암세포만 없애는 약을 연구하고 있어요.
examples.en: Doctors are researching a drug that destroys only cancer cells.
The new treatment attacks cancer cells.

examples.ko: 암세포의 크기가 작아져서 치료가 잘 되고 있대요.
examples.en: I heard the cancer cells have shrunk, so the treatment is going well.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 암세포를 찾는 인공지능 기술을 소개했어요.
examples.en: The news introduced AI technology that finds cancer cells.

explain: 병원 이야기에서 '암세포가 퍼지다', '암세포가 없어지다'처럼 쓰고, 보통 대화에서는 그냥 '암'이라고 짧게 말해요. 가까운 사람의 병 이야기는 조심스럽게 꺼내는 게 좋아요.

phrases.example: 이 치료는 암세포를 없애는 데 도움이 돼요.
phrases.en: This treatment helps get rid of cancer cells.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치료의 목적을 설명할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for explaining what a treatment is meant to do.

phrases.example: 암세포가 빨리 자라서 바로 수술해야 해요.
phrases.en: The cancer cells are growing fast, so surgery is needed right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 진행되는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how the disease is progressing.

phrases.en: My father had a cancer screening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 암세포보다 짧게 '암'이라고 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily conversation, people usually say the shorter 암 instead.

explain_en: In medical talk you say '암세포가 퍼지다' or '암세포가 없어지다', while in normal conversation people usually just say '암'. It is best to bring up a close person's illness carefully.

en: to become thin; to lose weight

examples.ko: 병을 앓고 나서 얼굴이 많이 여위었어요.
examples.en: After being ill, her face became very thin.

examples.ko: 요즘 밥을 못 먹어서 점점 여위어 가요.
examples.en: I can't eat these days, so I'm growing thinner.
Seeing his thin shoulders made my heart ache.
Grandmother has grown so thin that I'm worried.
The cat was thin, but its eyes were bright.
You look worn thin because of hard work.

explain: 병이나 고생 때문에 몸이 마르고 약해 보일 때 써서, 날씬해졌다는 칭찬과 달리 걱정하는 느낌이 있어요. 활용은 '여위어요, 여위었어요, 여윈'으로 해요.

phrases.example: 할머니의 여윈 얼굴을 보니 마음이 아팠어요.
phrases.en: Seeing Grandmother's thin face made my heart ache.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여위다'의 'ㄴ' 꾸밈형으로, 마른 얼굴이나 몸을 걱정하며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used when describing a thin face or body with concern.

phrases.en: You look much thinner these days, so I'm worried.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 말라 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone looks thin and worn.

phrases.example: 한 달 못 뵈었는데 많이 여위셨네요.
phrases.en: I haven't seen you for a month, and you've gotten much thinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 걱정하는 마음을 담아 높여 말하는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite, honorific form to an elder, with a tone of concern.

explain_en: For a person becoming thin and gaunt, often from tiredness or illness. It is used when someone gets thin and looks frail from illness or hardship, so it carries a worried feeling, unlike a compliment about being slim. The forms are '여위어요, 여위었어요, 여윈'.
